title: Emergency throughput regression: kernel scheduling + KV-eviction interaction
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported a sudden degradation in token throughput and increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC. Impacted traffic showed 2x-5x TTFT increases and tokens/sec drops for multi-turn chat workloads on both quantized and fp16 variants. This ticket coordinates the emergency triage, hotfix rollout, customer communications, and follow-up engineering work.
impact: Observed regressions across model families (large int4 and fp16 checkpoints) with highest impact on long-context multi-turn chats. Affected: Hosted API customers (high-volume chat apps), two Dedicated customers with reserved pools, and one Private on-prem deployment where GPU<->CPU spill behavior amplified the issue. Customer escalations received from: FinEdge (latency SLA breach), RetailVoice (product demos failing), and GovPartner (Private deployment).
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay a 4-turn chat with average prompt length 120 tokens and calls to streaming outputs. 2) Send sustained parallel requests (10-30 qps) with mixed sequence lengths. 3) Observe TTFT and tokens/sec on Grafana panels: /dashboard/db/throughput-metrics and host-level GPU mem pressure. Reproducible in staging with synthetic traffic using stress harness (tests/perf/harness/long-context).
root_cause_summary: Initial triage suggests a recent kernel selector heuristic change (stride and scheduling optimizer) that altered kernel packing for certain sequence-length distributions. Under expected batching the heuristic led to frequent kernel context switches and misaligned memory access patterns. Concurrently, a change to KV-cache eviction thresholds caused synchronous GC under bursty prefix reuse, triggering CPU-GPU memory copies on some Private nodes with constrained pinned memory. The interaction of both changes produced amplified TTFT and tokens/sec regressions under realistic workloads.
mitigation_applied:
- Rolled back kernel-scheduler heuristic in staging and queued emergency rollback to production (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2196).
- Deployed temporary conservative KV-cache eviction thresholds and made eviction async for Dedicated pools (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/578).
- Added per-tenant outgoing batch cap for Dedicated to limit pathological batch packing until proper fix lands.
- Updated routing policy to prefer low-latency model variant for Hosted customers during maintenance window.
outage_communication: Initial customer notifications sent 2026-03-09 09:15 UTC via support and account teams. Follow-up emails with mitigations posted 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC. Customer PMs alerted for FinEdge, RetailVoice, GovPartner with dedicated postmortem invitation. Slack incident channel: #inc-431221-throughput
next_steps: 1) Finalize kernel-selector fix: add sequence-length aware packing that respects KV cache locality (owner: Ravi). 2) Add async GC and fallbacks to prevent blocking copies on Private nodes (owner: Saniya Patel). 3) Expand stress tests in CI to include mixed-length multi-turn chat replay harness. 4) Create automated alert that correlates TTFT spike with KV GC events. 5) Schedule postmortem and include rollout checklist for runtime-1.26.0-hotfix.
